name: Example: Solving an Inequality Involving Exponential Functions with the Same Exponents and a Polynomial
worked_solution:
First, we move all the terms to the left side of the inequality and factor:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}{e}^{x+1}-2{e}^{x+1} & <-x{e}^{x+1} \\ {x}^{2}{e}^{x+1}+x{e}^{x+1}-2{e}^{x+1} & <0 \\ ({x}^{2}+x-2){e}^{x+1} & <0 \\ (x+2)(x-1){e}^{x+1} & <0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we divide both sides by $e^{x+1}$ and get

$$
(x+2)(x-1) <   0.
$$

This represents an upwards parabola whose roots are at $x=-2$ and $x=1.$ The parabola is below the $x$-axis when $-2 <   x <   1.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14013930/assets/2f01104ae0cb9a41c5c5e4b8393e346f7d0e9b2bfd1afa593ee6bdfb0fff39f2.png)

Therefore, the solution is $-2 <   x <   1.$
